AI spending is rapidly accelerating in the US.

US private fixed investment in information processing equipment and software grew at an annualized rate of +7.3% in Q3 2026, to a record $1.77 trillion.

This marks the largest quarterly increase since Q4 1983.

By comparison, at the height of the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble, this metric grew +6.2%.

Since Q4 2022, private fixed investment in information processing equipment and software has surged +61%, or +$671 billion.

As a % of GDP, this metric is up to a record 5.4%, significantly surpassing the previous high of 4.5% recorded in Q4 2000.

The scale of US AI investment is unlike anything seen before.

This is how our BuySide Open Interest changed on Friday. 

TLDR: net long.

Sum of the top 50 most-active names (est.): 
+$27.0B long delta, −$609M gamma per 1% move, +$8.6M vega per vol point.

$SPY & $QQQ long calls on net, while SPX biggest change was put shorts

Noticeable new net downside positioning:
$TSLA , $AAPL , $MSTR, $PLTR , $DRAM, $SKHY , $AMZN , $IBIT 

Bullish:
$NVDA , $SPCX , $META  , $HOOD , $INTC , $MU , $GOOGL 

Generally speaking, for this chart:
Positive delta: net short puts or net long calls.
Negative delta: net long puts or net short calls.

Positive gamma: net long options.
Negative gamma: net short options.

Positive vega: net long options, weighted toward near-the-money and longer-dated.
Negative vega: net short options, same weighting. Not a wings read.

The Equal-Weight Index surged +4.8% in October, while the S&P 500 fell -0.9%.

Year-to-date, the Equal-Weight Index has gained +13.9%, exceeding the S&P 500's +10.7% return as technology stocks lag the broader market.

Meanwhile, the S&P 500 ex-AI Index has jumped +14.2% year-to-date, reaching a new all-time high on Friday.

Market leadership is rapidly shifting.

tweets.text:
AI is burning Big Tech's free cash flow:

The combined CapEx of Amazon, $AMZN, Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, and Microsoft, $MSFT, rose +$36.9 billion in Q3 2026, to a record $201.9 billion.

This figure has more than doubled over the last 12 months and is up +356% since Q1 2024.

Big Tech has now spent $1.6 trillion on CapEx over the last 3 years.

Meanwhile, the combined free cash flow of these companies fell -$33.1 billion last quarter, to -$26.4 billion, its lowest on record.

Free cash flow among these firms has dropped -$88.2 billion over the last year.

Only Microsoft reported positive free cash flow in Q3.

Looking ahead, these 4 companies plan to spend another $232 billion on CapEx in Q4, potentially lifting their combined CapEx to a record $740 billion in 2026.

Big Tech is undertaking one of the largest infrastructure buildouts in history.

Obamacare was sold on a promise: premiums would fall $2,500 a year for the typical family.

Average individual premiums doubled in the first 4 years, and they are still climbing today.

Most of the 23 taxpayer-funded co-ops built under the law went bankrupt, burning roughly $2 billion. Enrollment is down 12% as insurers flee 31 states.

This was never a free market.

This is a subsidy-dependent program that needs bigger and bigger taxpayer checks in order for it to survive.

tweets.text: The S&P 500 fell 1.8% last Friday, its 22nd decline so far this year with a loss above 1%. tweets.text: Good Morning from Germany, where surging gas prices are sending electricity costs soaring. Day-ahead power hit €315/MWh on Wednesday, the highest since 2024. Year-ahead power is at €163/MWh, the highest since 2023. That’s 16.3 Cents/kWh before roughly 22 Cents in additional taxes and duties; implying a household price of around 38 Cents/kWh. An expensive winter looms.

Even backing that out, profits/profit margins are still rising.
tweets.quoted_tweet_text:
Amazon and Alphabet booked $233 billion of non-operating income over the last year, mostly gains on equity investments.

That's 9% of total profits for the 500 largest nonfinancial companies.

Back it out, and trailing profit margins are 14.1% instead of 15.4% for the big 500. https://t.co/xXNfJzb0Q5

tweets.text: I used to think this too until AI solved the Erdős conjecture. At this point, arguing that AI is simply synthesizing existing knowledge is like arguing that Einstein never really came up with General Relativity because he was simply synthesizing the work of Riemann, Poincare, etc.
tweets.quoted_tweet_text: Henry Farrell and Cosma Shalizi argue in the Economist that AI is not an incipient Digital God, but rather a "condensate of human culture": a statistical floor plan of Jacques Barzun's "House of Intellect," animated like an oral bard's repertoire of tropes. (1/4)

thread_tweets.text: One can think of the entire set of human knowledge as being bounded by a frontier. The question is “Does it really matter if an AI can’t jump from the frontier to a faraway point (novel knowledge) if the frontier itself can expand rapidly over time to eventually reach that point?”
